newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mainly firmer, gasoline steady.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mainly firmer, gasoline steady.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mainly firmer on Tuesday and gasoline held steady.

Naphtha ended $4 higher at $227/$229 cif after continued delays at Algeria's Skikda port kept four large cargoes waiting to be loaded. One end-user was shipping material from Tunisia to Antwerp due to the delays.
A port official said oil tankers may be allowed to berth on Wednesday based on better weather forecasts.
Gasoline held steady after recent crude gains and arbitrage interest to the U.S., particularly for cat cracked gasoline. Italian demand was also expected to pick up in December.
Crude's recent rise filtered through, plus market talk that Romania may be looking for upwards of 400,000 tonnes in Dec.
"They have a requirement, but there's the old question of whether they have the money," said one trader.
Buy tenders from Portugal and Turkey that closed on Tuesday for up to 125,000 tonnes into January also gave support to prices put at $111-113 fob Med.
A good quality bunker spec cargo was understood sold at around $124 cif. However, there are six ISAB cargoes available in December which will act as a counter balance.
Low sulphur cracked was also a touch firmer pegged around $145 cif Italy, but there was no visible buying interest.

Gas oil advanced $3 on futures, but heating oil remained long and premiums were under pressure at around cif high +$0.50 basis Genoa. Only one buyer was seen, bidding cif high -$1 for a parcel into Beirut.
A Russian flexi was reported done into Genoa cif high +$0.75 delivery December 12-20. A cargo of low sulphur diesel was sold at cif mean -$0.25 basis Genoa for delivery December 23-25.
Elsewhere interest focussed on a tender by India for a second purchase of high speed diesel for delivery in January.
